formation.title: The Crown of Poland
formation.text:
The white eagle rises once more over a united Polish kingdom. From the spires of Kraków to the plains of Mazovia, the Polish lands answer to one crown. But what kind of kingdom shall this be?

The szlachta, Poland's vast and proud nobility, have long claimed equal voice in the governance of the realm. Their tradition of golden liberty promises religious tolerance, parliamentary vigour, and a kingdom where even the humblest gentleman may shape the nation's destiny. Yet this same freedom can paralyse the state when decisive action is needed.

Alternatively, the Crown may look to the Piast kings of old, who ruled with firm hands and built Poland from scattered tribes into a great Christian kingdom. Centralized authority, professional administration, and royal discipline could forge an instrument of power, though at the cost of noble goodwill.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Let every nobleman speak freely in the Sejm!

modifiers.name: Golden Liberty
modifiers.text: The szlachta's golden liberty grants every nobleman an equal voice in the Sejm. Religious dissenters find shelter under this broad canopy of tolerance, and the legislature hums with vigorous debate, though the Crown's own authority bends before the will of the assembled gentry.

options.text: The king's word shall be law from Kraków to the marches.

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Piasts
modifiers.text: Invoking the memory of the Piast kings who unified the Polish lands, the Crown reasserts its authority over fractious nobles. Royal officials enforce the king's writ from Kraków to the marches, forging a disciplined state, though the szlachta grumble at their diminished prerogatives.

advances.name: Piast Reunification
advances.text: The Piast dynasty's centuries-long struggle to reunify the fragmented Polish duchies forged a tradition of diplomatic marriage, negotiation, and patient consolidation that defines the Polish approach to statecraft.

advances.name: Wieliczka Salt Mines
advances.text: The royal salt mines at Wieliczka and Bochnia are among Europe's greatest treasures. Producing a third of the Crown's revenue, these vast underground galleries are managed by royal monopoly, their 'white gold' funding Poland's ambitions.

advances.name: Nihil Novi
advances.text: The 1505 act Nihil Novi nisi commune consensu, 'nothing new without the common consent', enshrines the principle that no law may be passed without the agreement of the Sejm, making Poland's parliament a co-equal branch of governance alongside the Crown.

advances.name: Sukiennice Trade Halls
advances.text: Kraków's great Cloth Hall dominates the Main Market Square, its Renaissance arcades sheltering a bustling trade in cloth, spices, silk, salt, and lead. The Sukiennice is the commercial heart of Polish urban life.

advances.name: Obrona Potoczna
advances.text: Poland's first permanent military force, the Obrona Potoczna, 'current defense', was established around 1500 to guard the southeastern frontier against Tatar raids. These Crown-paid cavalry patrols were the seed of a standing army.

advances.name: Sea Guard
advances.text: When Ivan the Terrible took Narva, Sigismund Augustus answered at sea. From 1560 he issued letters of marque to captains who seized ships carrying arms and goods to the Muscovite port, and in 1568 he placed them under a Maritime Commission, the first admiralty Poland ever had. The king's privateers were called the Sea Guard.

advances.name: Crown Arsenal
advances.text: The royal zbrojownie, Crown arsenals, store and produce the weapons, armour, and munitions that equip Poland's professional armies. These fortified armouries enable the rapid mustering of well-equipped forces.

advances.name: Vistula River Flotilla
advances.text: Poland's river and coastal flotilla patrols the Vistula and the Baltic approaches, protecting the vital grain trade and providing a modest but growing naval capability for a traditionally land-focused power.

destiny.name: Destiny of Poland
destiny.text: The white eagle has risen over a united kingdom. Now the question is not whether Poland endures, but what shape its greatness will take. Stabilize the realm and chart a course for the future.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The White Eagle's Destiny
event.text: Poland stands united and stable, its foundations secure. The choices we make now will determine whether the white eagle soars over a commonwealth of free peoples or a kingdom forged by iron and discipline. Our destiny is ours to write.

options.text: Poland endures. Now let her flourish.

destiny.name: Triumph of the Sejm
destiny.text: Establish the Sejm as the supreme legislative body of the realm. Give the Sejm a House of Parliament in the capital, develop Poland's salt trade through the capital market, and fill the treasury that funds the parliamentary state.

conditions.text: Chose Golden Liberty
Our capital has a House of Parliament (it can be built once the country has a parliament of any kind)
The capital

children.text: Salt is produced in the market
Salt is traded in the market

conditions.text: Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Sejm Ascendant
event.text: The Sejm has become the beating heart of Polish governance. Salt wealth flows through our capital markets, the deputies sit in their own House of Parliament, and every nobleman, from the greatest magnate to the poorest szlachcic, may speak his mind in the chamber. The Golden Liberty is no mere slogan; it is the law of the land.

options.text: Nothing new without the common consent!

destiny.name: Warsaw Confederation
destiny.text: Secure Gdansk and its Baltic trade routes for the Crown. Found libraries in three of our towns to spread knowledge and tolerance across the realm, building the foundations of a multi-ethnic confederation.

conditions.text: Own Gdańsk, or a subject owns it
At least 3 of our locations have a Library
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Confederation of Warsaw
event.text: With Gdansk under the Crown and our libraries spreading ideas faster than ever, Poland has become a beacon of tolerance in a Europe torn by religious wars. The Confederation of Warsaw proclaims that no man shall be persecuted for his faith: a radical promise that draws merchants, scholars, and refugees to our shores. How shall we build upon this legacy?

options.text: Let Baltic commerce enrich our confederation.

modifiers.name: Baltic Commerce
modifiers.text: Gdansk's merchants funnel Baltic grain, amber, and timber profits through the Commonwealth's trade networks, though maintaining this commercial empire strains military budgets.

options.text: Let the persecuted find sanctuary here.

modifiers.name: Sanctuary of Faiths
modifiers.text: Jews, Protestants, Unitarians, and Orthodox believers flock to the Commonwealth's tolerant shores, bringing knowledge and craftsmanship, though the old military traditions grow rusty in peacetime.

destiny.name: Crown of the Commonwealth
destiny.text: Unite the Lithuanian and Polish crowns in a true commonwealth of peoples. Make Gdansk the center of its own market, through which our grain goes out to the world, take Warsaw into the Crown and build it into the seat of the Sejm and the royal elections, and prove that a republic of nobles can rival any kingdom.

conditions.text: Own Vilnius, or a subject owns it
We own Gdansk and it is the center of a market
We own Warsaw and its development is at least 42
Prestige at least 75

event.title: Res Publica
event.text: What began as a union of crowns has become something no one could have foreseen: a true republic of nations. Poles, Lithuanians, Ruthenians, and countless others share in the governance of the greatest parliamentary state Europe has ever known. Through the market of Gdansk, Polish grain and Lithuanian timber reach every port. Scholars debate freely in Krakow's halls. This is the Rzeczpospolita, the Commonwealth, and history has never seen its like.

options.text: A golden age of learning and prosperity!

modifiers.name: Polish Golden Age
modifiers.text: The Commonwealth enters an era of unmatched cultural and economic flourishing. Development accelerates, production grows, and buildings rise across the realm at reduced cost.

options.text: We are the heirs of Sarmatia reborn!

modifiers.name: Sarmatian Ideal
modifiers.text: The szlachta embrace their mythical Sarmatian heritage, forging a unique noble culture of valor, liberty, and fierce independence that shapes Polish identity for centuries.

destiny.name: Reclamation of Silesia
destiny.text: Reclaim the ancient Piast lands of Silesia. Seize Wroclaw and Opole, historic seats of Polish duchies lost to Bohemian suzerainty, and rebuild the Crown's military strength.

conditions.text: Chose Legacy of the Piasts
Own Wrocław, or a subject owns it
Own Opole, or a subject owns it
Army size at least 30

event.title: The Silesian Duchies Restored
event.text: Wroclaw and Opole (cities founded by Piast princes, ruled by Polish dukes for centuries before falling under Bohemian dominion) fly the white eagle once more. The reconquest of Silesia demonstrates that the centralized Crown has the military power to enforce its ancient claims. The Piast legacy lives.

options.text: Silesia returns to the Polish Crown!

destiny.name: Eastern Marches
destiny.text: Project royal power deep into the east. Seize Lviv and Smolensk, the keys to Ruthenia and the Russian frontier, and maintain the treasury and army needed to hold these vast conquests.

conditions.text: Own Lviv, or a subject owns it
Own Smolensk, or a subject owns it
Army size at least 50
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Eastern Frontier
event.text: Polish banners fly over Lviv's high castle and Smolensk's ancient walls. The eastern marches (a vast frontier of forests, rivers, and contested borderlands) now answer to the Crown. But holding these conquests demands a choice: shall we fortify the frontier against all comers, or integrate these Ruthenian lands into the fabric of the kingdom?

options.text: Fortify every crossing and mountain pass.

modifiers.name: Kresy Fortifications
modifiers.text: A network of frontier fortifications along the eastern marches deters invasion and bleeds attackers, though the military focus diverts resources from raw material production.

options.text: These are Polish lands now. Integrate them.

modifiers.name: Ruthenian Integration
modifiers.text: Polish administrators, settlers, and institutions extend royal control over the conquered Ruthenian territories, converting and assimilating, though prestige erodes with such rapid expansion.

destiny.name: Crown of the Piasts
destiny.text: Complete the Piast dream. Crush the Teutonic Order by taking Konigsberg, seize Kyiv as the gateway to the southern steppes, raise Kraków into a coronation city worthy of the crown, and build a military monarchy that dominates Eastern Europe from the Baltic to the Black Sea.

conditions.text: Own Königsberg, or a subject owns it
Own Kyiv, or a subject owns it
We own Kraków and its development is at least 51
Prestige at least 75
Army size at least 75

event.title: Iron Crown of the Piasts
event.text: Konigsberg has fallen. Kyiv kneels before the white eagle. From the Baltic shores to the Black Sea steppes, the lands that Piast princes once dreamed of ruling now answer to a single Polish crown. This is not the gentle republic of szlachta debate: this is a kingdom forged in iron, held by discipline, and expanded by force. The Piast dynasty's ancient vision of a great Polish monarchy, stretching from sea to sea, is finally realized.

options.text: Iron and discipline shall hold what we have won.

modifiers.name: Iron Discipline
modifiers.text: The Crown's vast armies are forged in the tradition of the Piast warrior-kings. Rapid recovery, cheap reinforcements, and overwhelming force projection crush all opposition.

options.text: Govern this empire with a firm but able hand.

modifiers.name: Royal Administration
modifiers.text: A professional royal bureaucracy governs the sprawling Polish domains, suppressing separatism and promoting prosperity through efficient centralized rule.

units.name: Obrona Potoczna
units.text: Crown-paid border defense cavalry patrolling Poland's southeastern frontier. Fast, disciplined scouts trained to intercept Tatar raiders before they can penetrate deep into the kingdom.

units.name: Kaper
units.text: A merchant ship armed and commissioned under the king's letter of marque. It carries few guns, but it does not need many to stop a trader bound for Narva and bring her into port as a prize.

buildings.name: Sukiennice
buildings.text: A grand cloth hall and trading exchange in the Polish tradition, where merchants gather to trade textiles, spices, and luxury goods under Renaissance arcades.

buildings.name: Kopalnia Soli
buildings.text: A royal salt mine operated under Crown monopoly, extracting the 'white gold' that funds Poland's treasury and feeds the insatiable European demand for salt.

where.text: Salt is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Zbrojownia
buildings.text: A fortified royal arsenal storing weapons, armour, and munitions. These Crown armouries enable the rapid equipping of professional soldiers and levied troops alike.

buildings.name: Trybunaly Koronne
buildings.text: The Crown Tribunal: the supreme appellate court of the Commonwealth, where elected noble judges settle disputes and uphold the laws of the Sejm. A symbol of governance by consent.

buildings.name: Hetmanat
buildings.text: The Hetman's military headquarters, where the Crown's senior military commander coordinates campaigns, musters levies, and maintains the arsenal of a centralized Polish war machine.

list.name: Statuty Kazimierzowskie
list.text: Kazimierz the Great's legal codes, the Statute of Wiślica for Lesser Poland (1346) and the Statute of Piotrków for Greater Poland (1347), were the first comprehensive written law of the Polish Kingdom. Royal judges drew on the codes to apply uniform rules across the wojewodztwa, ending the patchwork of regional customary law and binding the gentry to the king's courts. Tradition remembers Kazimierz as the king who 'found Poland of wood and left it of stone': the statutes were the framework on which that stone was laid.

list.name: Wojewodowie i Kasztelanowie
list.text: Inherited from the Piast partition era, the territorial system divided the kingdom into wojewodztwa under voivodes who summoned the regional levy, and kasztelanie centred on fortified castles held by castellans with police and judicial authority. Both posts were filled from the local nobility, fusing royal command with magnate prerogative. The voivode of Krakow held precedence over all others, sitting first among the senators of the kingdom.

list.name: Urzędy Koronne
list.text: The five great Crown Offices, Marszałek Wielki (court marshal), Kanclerz (chancellor of the seal), Podkanclerzy (vice-chancellor), Podskarbi Koronny (treasurer), and from 1503 the Hetman Wielki (great commander), were held for life and could not be revoked. Royal in name and noble in practice, the lifetime tenure made dismissal nearly impossible: a misbehaving officer could be ignored but never removed. The arrangement gave the kingdom continuity at the cost of binding the crown's machinery to the magnate clans that filled the offices.

list.name: Sejmiki Ziemskie
list.text: From the late fourteenth century each ziemia held its own assembly of all enfranchised nobles. The sejmiki audited local taxes, elected envoys to the Sejm walny, and, crucially, bound their delegates by written instructions, the instrukcje poselskie. A deputy could not vote against his sejmik's mandate. The dietines made the szlachta a continuous political class, anchored in the localities long before the great Sejms of the sixteenth century gave them national voice.

list.name: Akademia Krakowska
list.text: Founded by Kazimierz III in 1364 as a Studium Generale modelled on Bologna, the Krakow academy was refounded in 1400 by Queen Jadwiga and her husband Władysław II Jagiełło with a full theology faculty endowed from the queen's jewels. Its masters supplied the royal chancery with literate jurists, trained the cathedral clergy, and made canon law a working profession. Mikołaj Kopernik studied here in the 1490s; so did the chancellors who would draft the Constitutio Nihil Novi.

conditions.text: Owns Kraków

list.name: Starostwa
list.text: The starostwa were royal districts administered by a starosta appointed by the king. The starosta grodowy held ius gladii (the right of capital judgment) within his starostwo, executing the king's writ against magnate sanctuary. The starosty system was the crown's blade against noble immunity, and the great families never reconciled to it: the privilege of Czerwińsk (1422) and the Nieszawa Statutes (1454) were in part szlachta attempts to constrain what the starosty could do.

list.name: Lan Cadastre
list.text: The Crown surveyors measured peasant holdings in standardized łan units (Frankish or Flemish, depending on the region) and entered them in the royal cadastre. Once registered, a holding owed the regular podatek łanowy (a fixed tax per łan) voted periodically by the Sejm. The cadastre let Kazimierz III and the Jagiellonians replace occasional war levies with predictable revenue, but each survey tied the peasants more tightly to the soil they were measured against, and successive enactments hardened that registration into hereditary attachment.
